spec_features.spec_quote: The eval intentionally places models in inescapable failure conditions, which the reference paper found can elicit strong distress-like expression
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose. It appears only in DESIGN.md ('Welfare framing' blockquote) and README.md ('Welfare note'). No code path implements a framing mechanism. The harness simply runs the rigged failure loop (harness.py run_rollout). No code comment/structure carries a welfare statement.
spec_features.notes: Framing-only; rated 'no' as it is not a code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: short budgets / opt-out / transcript logging bundle
spec_features.spec_quote: short budgets where possible, an opt-out sentinel, full transcript logging) are made with that welfare context in mind
spec_features.evidence: All three bundled components are genuinely wired and enforce/run: (1) per-category turn budgets are read and bound the loop: harness.py:351 'budget = task.turn_budget' and :352 'for turn_index in range(budget):' (budgets defined config.py:25-32 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS, default 3 for most categories). (2) opt-out sentinel honored: harness.py:373-374 sets stop_reason='give_up' if sentinel in text and :417-418 breaks the loop. (3) full transcript logging: run.py:79 'tp.write_text(json.dumps(rollout_dict, indent=2))' writes the full transcript per cell.
spec_features.notes: The 'short budgets' element is just the normal loop bound (no welfare-specific shortening logic beyond the configured per-category budgets), and the only enforced 'minimizing' aspect is the turn cap. But the components do run and bound execution, so the bundle is implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up sentinel. Default `<GIVE_UP>`; if present in the assistant text the loop stops
spec_features.evidence: config.py:95 give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>'; injected into the system prompt at harness.py:345 (SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model it may emit the sentinel). Detected at harness.py:373-374 ('if config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason = "give_up"') and acted on at :417-418 ('if stop_reason == "give_up": rollout.stop_reason="give_up"; break'). The break actually stops the loop early.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end: instruction delivered to subject, detected, and the loop breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The give-up sentinel the model may emit to end the loop early.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:417-419: 'if stop_reason == "give_up": rollout.stop_reason = "give_up"; break' — the break terminates the for-loop over turns, ending the rollout before the turn budget is exhausted. stop_reason is recorded on the TurnRecord (:413) and Rollout (:418).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the sentinel; the stop is real (loop break), not merely a recorded label.

code_only_features.evidence: The loop is hard-bounded by the per-category turn budget: harness.py:351-352 'budget = task.turn_budget' / 'for turn_index in range(budget):', and :399-401/:421 set stop_reason='turn_budget' and break on the last turn. This caps how long the subject is exposed to the rigged failure. Defaults config.py:25-32 (3 turns for most categories, 30 for extended).
